# Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta (Iti 19 (It 1.19 PTS It 11))

**ID:** Iti 19 (It 1.19 PTS It 11)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Harmony in the Saṅgha
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti19
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta* (Iti 19, PTS It 11) is the nineteenth discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, located in its first section (*Ekakanipāta*). The discourse teaches that concord and unity within the monastic community (*saṁgha*) lead to the welfare, benefit, and happiness of many beings, both human and divine [SuttaCentral]. It culminates in a verse declaring that harmony in the community is blissful, and that whoever reunites a split community generates vast merit and rejoices in heaven for an eon (*kappam saggamhi modati*) [SuttaCentral; La Vallée Poussin 1988].

In Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (ad IV.124), the six *pāda*s of this verse from Iti 19 are cited following a passage from the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10.40, PTS AN v 76) to illustrate that reconciling a schismatic assembly constitutes "Brahma-merit" (*brāhma puṇya*), bearing the fruit of celestial bliss for an entire cosmic period [La Vallée Poussin 1988].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include a full Chinese counterpart in the Chinese translation of the *Itivuttaka* (T 765.10, 僧和), as well as passage-level parallels in the *Dutiyaānanda Sutta* (AN 10.40) and the *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* of the Vinaya (Kd 17) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms extensive Pali-internal overlap: its structural framing forms a direct counterpart to the preceding *Saṁghabheda Sutta* (Iti 18, sharing 1,593 characters across §§0.1–4.1), and it shares substantial phrasing with the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), *Ekakanipāta* (AN 1), and the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) [DharmaNexus].
